desc: Write a brute-force program to enumerate all orientations of G for small N (3,4,5) and all s, count distinct in-degree sequences, and tabulate results.
Run the brute-force script and capture its output.
Analyze the output: check if for fixed (N,k) all strings give the same count, or if it depends on structure (runs, gaps, circular adjacency of 1s).
Based on analysis, hypothesize a closed-form formula (likely involves N, k, and the number of "blocks" of consecutive 1s, or the number of "isolated" 1s, etc.).
Prove the formula using the cut-condition / polymatroid characterization (Fulkerson–Chen–Anstee theorem) and decompose the problem into the cycle part and the apex part.
Derive an O(N) algorithm (or O(N log MOD)) using the formula, computing factorials/powers mod 998244353.
Implement the final solution and test against provided samples (N=3,s=010 → 14; N=20 sample → 261339902).
Stress test on edge cases: N=3 all s, N=10^6 all 0, N=10^6 all 1, random s, and verify with brute force for small N.
